outcome.answer: Several of the supplied papers use self-play reinforcement learning to train agents for strategy games. One approach trains a transformer policy with plain policy-gradient self-play on sparse win/loss reward for Generals.io (a real-time strategy game), with an ablation showing an exponential moving average deployment policy and training only on highest-advantage samples for better performance [1]. Another adapts AlphaZero-style self-play to Tablut, modifying the architecture to use separate policy/value heads for each player role and stabilizing training with data augmentation, replay buffer changes, and a portion of games against randomly sampled past checkpoints [2]. For games with large hidden information, Ataraxos applies self-play reinforcement learning and test-time search under hidden information, achieving superhuman results in Stratego and extending to other games including Hanabi and dou dizhu [3].
